findings.title: PropertyResourceBundle read with default ISO-8859-1 encoding corrupts non-ASCII translations
findings.body: The verifier opens the properties file with FileInputStream and constructs PropertyResourceBundle, which decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1. Message properties files are UTF-8 encoded (as read correctly earlier with Files.readString), so all non-ASCII characters will be misdecoded. This will produce garbled strings, causing false positives in HTML detection and possibly invalid characters, making the verifier unreliable for most translated files. Use an InputStreamReader with UTF-8 or a Reader-based PropertyResourceBundle constructor.

findings.body: The value for totpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This will display Italian text to Lithuanian users. The original text was Lithuanian. The same issue occurs in the login theme file.

findings.title: Blanket removal of style attribute based on path containing 'email' is fragile
findings.body: The normalization removes any occurrence of ' style="direction: rtl;"' for any file whose absolute path contains the substring 'email'. This is not specific to email message files; it can affect other resources in directories with 'email' in the name, silently removing legitimate style attributes. It also only matches the exact string, so variations like single quotes or no spaces will not be removed, leading to false positives. Replace with a precise check or handle styles in the sanitizer policy.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException if English reference file is missing
findings.body: When constructing englishFile and opening it with FileInputStream, any IOException is wrapped in a RuntimeException. If a translation file has no corresponding English file (e.g., some community-only resources), the verifier will abort the entire build. This should be handled gracefully, perhaps by skipping HTML verification or reporting a specific error message, not crashing.
